page.running_head: Sect. I. Part. I. Cap. XXV.

main_text.head: Ἔκθεσις.[?]
main_text.p: Sic rota & trochus in orbem volvuntur.
Hactenus motus è causis simplex: Mistus est par-tim per se, partim per accidens, unde medius appellatur.
main_text.head: Ἔκθεσις.[?]
main_text.p: Hujusmodi lapidis motus est, cum magna vi de-orsum jacitur: per se enim est, ratione loci, quem pe-tit per virtutem motricem naturalem: per accidens vero, ratione celeri-tate: Majori enim fertur celeritate, quam vi sua & pondere per naturam ferretur. Refertur huc quoque motus progressivus animalis. Per accidens enim est, ratione corporis, quod natura sua deorsum fertur,per se vero, ratione animæ.
Hucusque distributio motus è causis:ex effectis seu terminis ad quos, qui tres potissimum sunt: Quantitas: qualitas: locus: motus quoque in tres species distribuitur.
Prima species pro termino ad quem habet quantitatem maiorem vel minorem.
Cuius terminus ad quem quantitas maior est, Augmentatio appellatur, quæ motus est à minori quantitate ad maiorem.

page.notes: The left strip shows the edge of the facing printed page with marginal text; it is not transcribed, as it belongs to the neighbouring page. The Greek titles above and below the paragraph are small and uncertain; the first is read as Ἔκθεσις, with [?]. The catchword "Hu-" is at the right below the last line and is kept as printed; "I." is taken as the gathering signature. The bare-number headings XXIX to XXXII are copied as paragraphs by rule. Possible spelling "Hactenus" is read from the scan with ct ligature, not checked against another copy.
